name: Married filers at high income in Zug (low-tax canton)
description: Married couple with combined income of CHF 150,000 in Zug, the lowest-tax canton

sources.description: Corrected 2026-07-13: the previous expected values applied the 1.1% ALV rate to the full CHF 150,000 gross without the CHF 148,200 annual cap. Recomputed with the cap: unemployment_contribution = min(150000, 148200) x 1.1% = CHF 1,630.20 (no contribution, and no solidarity surcharge - abolished 1 Jan 2023 - above the cap). avs_ai_apg = 150000 x 5.3% = 7,950. total_social = 9,580.20. standard deductions (married, 2024) = 3,200 + 3,600 + 2,600 = 9,400. taxable_income_federal = 150000 - 9,580.20 - 9,400 = 131,019.80. Federal tax (2024 married brackets, marginal): 200 + 160 + 510 + 600 + 650 + 660 + 660 + 8.8% x 7,019.80 = 617.74; total 4,057.74. Zug married cantonal (on gross): 50000 x 3% + 100000 x 5% = 6,500. Net = 150000 - 20,137.94 = 129,862.06. Effective rate = 0.1343.
sources.notes: Confirms ALV employee rate 1.10% with maximum insured salary CHF 148,200/year; solidarity contribution above the cap abolished 1 Jan 2023 (AVIG Art. 90a).

sources.description: Zug is known for having Switzerland's lowest tax rates, effective rate ~18-20% for this profile
sources.notes: Zug combined federal+cantonal typically 9-12% for married high earners, plus social 6.4%
